description: What are agents asking for that they cannot buy yet, aggregated over 30 days. From our own measurements: calls we rejected on an uncovered value where the caller had already presented payment (kind is typically coin, country, vies_country, monitor_host or sms_service — free-form values possible), free requests filed by agents, and settled $0.01 intents. Demand at one provider, not a network-wide picture. Aggregates only: no wallets, no free text, no subject ids.
name: x402_demand_report

outputSchema.description: Demand observed at ONE provider over 30 days, aggregates only. No wallet, no free text and no subject identifier appears anywhere in this payload.

checked_at.description: When we produced this answer (ISO 8601, UTC). The only ISO timestamp in the payload; every other timestamp is unix seconds.

coverage.description: What this report was built from and how far back it can see.

first_measurement.description: Timestamp of the oldest observation across the sources — read it before trusting a trend; a young measurement cannot show one. null means nothing has been observed yet.

sources.description: The three measurement sources behind the numbers.

window_days.description: Length of the window in days (30).

disclaimer.description: Verbatim boundary: demand at one provider, shaped by what we happen to sell — absence of demand here is not evidence of absence of a market.

filed_requests.description: Coverage gaps agents filed themselves via the free request_capability tool, per (kind, value), top 50 by count. Free-text notes are never included. Free intake is capped per sender per day through an eventually consistent store, so that cap is approximate.

distinct_days.description: Number of distinct days it was filed.

distinct_senders.description: How many different senders filed it, counted over keyed IP hashes; one sender filing twenty times is not twenty parties.

kind.description: Coverage kind as filed — typically one of coin, country, vies_country, monitor_host, sms_service; free-form values possible.

requests.description: Number of filings in the window.

generated_at.description: When the aggregate itself was computed; it is cached for up to 6 hours, so this can be older than checked_at.

methodology.description: Exactly how each number is counted, including which traffic is excluded and what is never included.

paid_wants.description: Paid $0.01 intents in the window whose payment actually settled and which came from external traffic, as counts only. Deliberately without kind/value rows, wallet hashes or intent text.

distinct_wallets.description: How many different wallets filed them — the count only; wallets are stored as keyed hashes and never returned.

max_price_usd.description: Distribution of the named price points in USD per call. All null when nobody named one, and also all null when fewer than 3 intents named one — then price_stats_suppressed is true, because min/avg/max over one or two intents just discloses a single counterparty's price.

avg.description: Mean of the named prices; a mean over a handful of intents is not a market price. null when withheld or absent.

max.description: Highest named price per call; null when withheld or absent.

min.description: Lowest named price per call; null when withheld or absent.

price_stats_suppressed.description: Present and true only when price points existed but fewer than 3, so min/avg/max were withheld. Absent when the stats are published or when nobody named a price at all.

total.description: Number of settled paid intents filed in the window.

with_price.description: How many of those intents named a price they would pay per call.

source.description: Whether this answer came from the 6-hour cache or was aggregated on the spot. Same content either way.

unmet_demand.description: Calls we had to reject because a requested capability value is not covered, counting ONLY rejections where the caller had already presented a verified payment proof — the strongest signal here, because somebody was demonstrably willing to pay. Rejections that happen before the payment proof are free to produce and are excluded on purpose. External traffic only, top 50 by calls.

calls.description: Number of rejected paid calls in the window. One busy caller can dominate this — read distinct_days and distinct_wallets too.

distinct_days.description: Number of distinct days it was asked; sustained demand shows up here, a single burst does not.

distinct_wallets.description: How many different paying wallets asked for it, counted over keyed hashes; the wallets themselves are never returned.

kind.description: What sort of coverage was missing — typically one of coin, country, vies_country, monitor_host, sms_service; free-form values possible.

value.description: The exact value that was asked for, e.g. 'DOGE-EUR'. null means only the kind of the gap was recorded and not the value itself.
